Now I'll calculate the track durations, classify them by length, and analyze the revenue by category. Let me start by examining the data distribution to determine the boundaries for short, medium, and long classifications.

args.sql:
SELECT 
  MIN(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 AS min_seconds,
  AVG(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 AS avg_seconds,
  MAX(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 AS max_seconds,
  MIN(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 AS min_minutes,
  AVG(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 / 60.0 AS avg_minutes,
  MAX(Milliseconds) / 1000.0 / 60.0 AS max_minutes
FROM Track

content: Now I'll calculate the track durations, classify them by length, and analyze the revenue by category.

args.sql:
WITH track_durations AS (
  SELECT 
    TrackId,
    Milliseconds / 1000.0 / 60.0 AS duration_minutes,
    CASE 
      WHEN Milliseconds / 1000.0 / 60.0 <= 197.34 THEN 'Short'
      WHEN Milliseconds / 1000.0 / 60.0 <= 2840.28 THEN 'Medium'
      ELSE 'Long'
    END AS category
  FROM music.Track
),
category_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    category,
    MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_time_minutes,
    MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_time_minutes,
    SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue
  FROM (
    SELECT 
      td.TrackId,
      td.category,
      SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS revenue
    FROM track_durations td
    JOIN music.InvoiceLine il ON td.TrackId = il.TrackId
    GROUP BY td.TrackId, td.category
  ) track_revenue
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT 
  category,
  MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_time_minutes,
  MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_time_minutes,
  total_revenue
FROM category_stats
